subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: What supported bootstrap shape should OpenClaw expose for local daemon, dashboard auth, and Telegram owner setup while preserving Telegram pairing and owner trust?
rationale: The remaining gap is not a missing helper call only; it chooses a public setup contract and security posture for first-owner Telegram access.

options.title: Add secure owner-allowlist bootstrap
options.body: Expose a first-class onboard or bootstrap path that installs or refreshes the daemon, emits the dashboard token URL, stores the Telegram bot token, resolves or accepts a numeric owner ID, and writes allowlist/preapproval state without unattended pairing approval.

options.title: Keep pairing explicit with documented composition
options.body: Document a supported command sequence that automates install, daemon, dashboard, and Telegram token setup but deliberately stops before owner authorization when numeric owner input is unavailable.

options.title: Defer broad bootstrap to narrower issues
options.body: Resolve Telegram default policy, post-bootstrap DM defaults, and pairing approval ergonomics separately through #7679, #81876, and #45839 instead of adding a combined bootstrap surface now.

recommendation.title: Add secure owner-allowlist bootstrap
recommendation.body: Expose a first-class onboard or bootstrap path that installs or refreshes the daemon, emits the dashboard token URL, stores the Telegram bot token, resolves or accepts a numeric owner ID, and writes allowlist/preapproval state without unattended pairing approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Dashboard/setup history and the security-sensitive product shape make this a cross-surface decision rather than a single Telegram implementation detail.
